title: State v. Carty (N.J. 2002)
key_points: Holding: Before asking for consent to search a lawfully stopped motor vehicle, the officer must have reasonable and articulable suspicion that the search will reveal evidence of a crime.
officer_notes: Scenario: A routine speeding stop with nothing suspicious, and you ask to search the car.
Takeaway: No reasonable suspicion, no consent request on a vehicle stop.
